request.spec:
A steward can merge a grade into another (two selects and a button; GRADE_MERGED from=<grade>
into=<grade>; the same grade twice, or anyone else, is refused): every person whose grade in force
today is the merged grade is given the other from the sheet's today, each exactly as the person
form would (PERSON_EDITED and the rollup lines, in list order).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can merge a grade into another (two selects and a button; GRADE_MERGED from=<grade>
into=<grade>; the same grade twice, or anyone else, is refused): every person whose grade in force
today is the merged grade is given the other from the sheet's today, each exactly as the person
form would (PERSON_EDITED and the rollup lines, in list order).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Grade merge is in, and all 4 tests pass when run with `bin/e2e`. That's the new grade-merge test plus the three scenario tests of existing behaviour.

**How it works**
- **Server:** there's a new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/grades/merge` (`grades/merge.POST.yml`). It refuses viewers and archived sheets as other changes do. It also refuses anyone who isn't a steward, the same grade twice, and merging into a retired grade. A refusal returns 422 and stores and records nothing.
- **Editing people:** `MergeGrade` writes `GRADE_MERGED from=… into=…`. It then goes through the people in list order, and anyone whose grade in force today is the merged grade is given the other grade from the sheet's today. Each edit runs through the person form's own `ApplyPerson` and `AuditPersonEdited`, so it writes the same `PERSON_EDITED` and rollup lines as a save in the form.
- **Front end:** the Grades panel has two selects (`grade-merge-from`, `grade-merge-into`) and a `grade-merge` button. When a merge is done, `grade-merged` shows e.g. `A into B: 1`. Refusals show `grade-error`, which clears as soon as either select changes or the button is pressed again.

**Things worth knowing**
- **Rollup lines appear twice.** The test expects Ada's `ROLLUP`/`TOTALS` lines twice after the A→B merge. Each person's edit writes its own rollup lines, and then the endpoint writes them once more for the merge as a whole. Merging C into B moved no figures, so it writes only `PERSON_EDITED`, which matches the test.
- **One refused person refuses the whole merge.** If any person's edit is refused (a name or alias clash, say), nothing is merged. To keep refused merges out of the audit file, I added a small `Audit.Buffer` to `Audit.java`: it holds a change's lines and writes them only if the whole change succeeds. Undoing the store writes relies on the request's transaction rolling back when the edit fails. No test covers that case, so I haven't run it.
- **`grade-merged` text includes the grades.** The test helper only accepts a merge once that text changes, so a bare count would make two merges that each move one person look the same. A repeat of the identical merge (same grades, same count) would still look the same.
- **Every screen refreshes after a merge.** All cached data is refetched, because a merge can change any figure on the sheet.
